title: Telemetry-driven kernel selector: token-density & thermal headroom model
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Reduce 95th/99th token latency tails on mixed-SKU, MIG-partitioned inference fleets by routing prefill and decode requests to the best-fit microkernel at request time. We will build a lightweight telemetry-driven model that predicts the preferred kernel variant using features derived from token-density, expected max_tokens, KV-cache reuse, current GPU clock headroom and per-slice thermal sensors.

Background: The runtime currently uses a static heuristic for kernel selection (sequence-length buckets + SKU table). This works for steady-state workloads but produces tail spikes when a stream of high-token-density requests hits a thermal-constrained MIG slice or when mixed-sku batches are packed suboptimally. Operators have experimented with reactive clock steering and coarse-grained fallbacks; early telemetry suggests kernel-choice errors correlate with token-density and instantaneous clock headroom.

Success metrics: 
- Reduce 95th token latency by >= 12% and 99th by >= 18% on our mixed H100/L40S/A10 test harness under the 'variable-chat' workload. 
- No more than 2% regression in average throughput for throughput-optimized flows. 
- Model inference overhead <= 300us per request in the hot path.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Offline model demonstrates improvement on historical traces (compare to baseline heuristic) and passes k-fold validation.
- A/B rollout on a small Dedicated pool shows latency tail reductions without throughput regressions. 
- Implementation merged with an integration test that injects synthetic thermal/clock signals and validates fallback behavior.

Design approach: 
1) Data collection: expand runtime telemetry to emit per-request features: token_density_histogram (buckets as counts), request_seq_len, max_tokens, kv_cache_hit_ratio, batch_size, gpu_clock_current_mhz, gpu_clock_nominal_mhz, per_slice_temp_celsius, mig_slice_id, sku_label (h100/l40s/a10), nvlink_bandwidth_util, timestamp. Store to compressed telemetry tables for ML training.
2) Feature engineering: derive normalized_token_density, clock_headroom_pct = (current/nominal), temp_headroom = (max_safe_temp - current_temp), recent_failure_rate for slice.
3) Model: lightweight tree ensemble (XGBoost/LightGBM) trained to predict expected token-latency delta between candidate kernels. Output: rank of kernel variants or binary decision to use fallback kernel. Model exported as a small decision graph for fast runtime evaluation.
4) Integration: Add a "kernel_hint" hook in prefill scheduling that invokes the model synchronously (fallback to cached heuristic on timeout). Ensure the call path runs in the scheduler thread with microsecond budget; consider moving evaluation to fast C++ runtime path or using a tiny decision table compiled into code.
5) Rollout plan: offline validation -> canary on 1 Dedicated pool (low-traffic) -> expand to mixed fleet -> monitor.

Open questions / trade-offs: 
- How to balance model complexity vs. runtime overhead? (we aim for sub-300us latency).
- Whether to include nvlink util and inter-slice congestion features; collecting these increases telemetry volume.
- Risk of model overfitting to particular request distributions; mitigation: continuous retraining with sliding window and conservative fallback policies.

comments: 2026-02-28: Triage notes: PM and runtime leads agreed this has medium customer impact and cross-sku priority. Agreed to scope as P1 experiment for runtime-2.1.

2026-03-02: Collected two weeks of telemetry from canary fleet (mixed H100/L40S/A10). Initial feature set validated; token_density_histogram and clock_headroom correlate with tail latency in correlation analysis (r=0.46 and r=0.61 respectively). Notebook: drive link above.

2026-03-04: Engineering decision: prototype model as XGBoost and export a compiled decision graph to the runtime C++ path to avoid Python IPC overhead. Marco to own runtime hook; Aisha to own training pipeline and dataset curation.
2026-03-06: PR created for telemetry schema changes (runtime repo): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821 — adds per_slice_temp and clock_headroom fields. CI pending.

2026-03-08: Offline model training completed on 50k trace windows. XGBoost (depth 5, 200 trees) reduces predicted 99th token latency by 22% vs heuristic on validation set. Saved model: s3://redwood-telemetry/models/eng-271900/v1.xgb

2026-03-10: Performance review: native C++ inference of exported decision graph measured at ~120us on p95 on a controlled host. Good headroom for scheduler. Created integration spike: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4855 (kernel-hint-hook).

2026-03-12: Blocker noted: some MIG slices do not expose per-slice temp sensors on older firmware; we will fallback to GPU-level temp and mark features as missing. Follow-up ticket opened to track firmware rollouts (ENG-271901).
2026-03-12: Next steps: finish integration tests, add synthetic thermal-injection tests, coordinate canary rollout for 2026-03-18. Planning a short demo for infra weekly on 2026-03-15.
